name: Persuasive / Argumentative Essay
purpose: Takes a position on a debatable issue and moves the reader toward agreeing with it or acting on it.

components.note: Must be an arguable claim, not a stated fact — this is what distinguishes it from the expository thesis.
Reasons for the claim, each backed by supporting evidence.
Present in persuasive writing; typically absent from purely argumentative/academic argument essays.

pitfalls: A strawman counterargument — refuting a weak version of the opposing view instead of its strongest form.
Evidence given with no explicit link back to the claim it's supposed to support.
A thesis that's actually a statement of fact, leaving nothing to argue.
